title: regional-surge-quarantine-and-transparent-trim-orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design and implement a regional surge quarantine controller that transparently trims non-critical request payloads and routes overflow to insulated circuits during multi-region stress. This ticket ties SLO-aware admission, regional isolation, and circuit breaker integration into a single orchestrator that operators can configure per-tenant and per-route.

Background: We currently have several ad-hoc soft-degrade mechanisms (early truncation, regional failover, and per-tenant token buckets) that operate independently. During a cross-region outage we observed cascading throttles where routing failover overloaded a single region and affected high-value tenants. Operators need a predictable, auditable way to quarantine surging regions, shed load with fidelity awareness, and keep critical SLO surfaces intact.

Scope:
- Implement a controller that can: quarantine an affected region for a configurable window, apply transparent trim policies on request payloads (e.g., token truncation, reply-length caps, feature toggles), and wire into existing circuit breakers so that downstream model pools are insulated from overflow.
- Provide admin APIs to configure per-tenant quarantine thresholds and per-route trim profiles.
- Emit detailed telemetry (decision reason, pre/post token counts, region tag, circuit state) for post-incident analysis and SLO alignment.
- Ensure minimum latency overhead for fast-path requests by keeping checks lightweight and cache-friendly.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can detect region surge using occupancy and error-rate signals and enter quarantine within 30s of threshold breach.
Transparent trim profiles applied without changing canonical request schema; clients receive metadata that indicates trimming occurred.
Circuit breaker integration prevents >95% of quarantine-triggered requests from reaching overloaded model pools (observed in chaos test).
Per-tenant SLO priorities respected: P0 tenants remain routed to a failover pool where possible; P2/P3 tenants are subject to progressive trimming and optional denial.
Dashboard shows quarantine events, trimmed token counts, and affected tenants with links to traces and PRDs.
Automated canary rollout: 0->5->25->100% with rollback if 99th percentile latency increases by >20% or error rate increases by >2x.
E2E chaos tests simulate cross-region failover and validate that critical SLOs stay within defined error budgets while non-critical requests are shed.
decision_log: 2026-02-12 - Chose quarantine window model (sliding 5m by default) over permanent routing changes to allow automatic recovery and minimize manual ops.
2026-02-20 - Selected transparent trimming (request annotation + conservative token removal) over aggressive rejection to preserve downstream model context where possible.
2026-02-25 - Integrated with existing circuit-breaker API instead of building a parallel breaker; reduces duplication and leverages current metrics pipeline.
2026-03-05 - Decided to expose per-tenant policy overrides in Console rather than forcing YAML-only configuration to enable rapid SRE response.
implementation_steps: Instrument region occupancy and error-rate signals as inputs to the quarantine evaluator (ENG infra metric adapters).
Create quarantine controller service with fast-path decision cache and async emit of telemetry to observability pipeline.
Implement transparent trim engine: token-aware prefix preservation, heuristic priority for system prompts, and per-route trim profiles.
Wire controller into circuit-breaker API to trigger 'insulate' mode for impacted model pools.
Add admin APIs and Console surface to view/adjust quarantine thresholds and per-tenant overrides.
Write unit tests, integration tests, and chaos scenarios for cross-region surge and failback behavior.
Run canary rollout with SRE on-call and monitor telemetry dashboards during ramp.
Post-mortem and iterative tuning after initial canary.
monitoring_playbook: Primary metrics: regional occupancy %, regional 5m error rate, trimmed_token_count, quarantine_events/sec, insulated_circuit_trips.
SLO checks: ensure P0 request success rate >= 99.95% and p99 latency within baseline during quarantine window.
Alerts: quarantine entered and >2% of total traffic trimmed for >3m => P0 oncall alert; circuit trips >3 in 10m => immediate paging.
Dashboards: per-region timeline with quarantine overlays, per-tenant trimmed tokens, top trimmed routes, and heatmap of circuit states.
Runbook steps: identify root cause region, evaluate overflow path, adjust quarantine thresholds or promote additional capacity, rollback if canary thresholds violated.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Unit/integration tests + feature flags behind operator-only API (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Internal canary on non-critical tenants with telemetry validation (1 week).
Phase 3: Limited external canary for <5% traffic, SRE monitor with extended retention of quarantine traces (1 week).
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 100% with metric-based gating and automated rollback hooks (2 weeks).
Post-rollout: tune default thresholds based on observed traffic patterns and add pre-baked profiles for common tenant classes.
testing_notes: Create synthetic surge generator that mimics simultaneous cross-region failover (route-level).
Add unit tests for trim engine to validate semantic-aware truncation of system vs user tokens.
Include tests for idempotency of quarantine decisions and for telemetry emission under load.
Chaos engineering: introduce packet loss and elevated queue latencies in region B to verify quarantine and graceful recovery.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-trimming could introduce silent quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative defaults + automatic A/B evaluation against heldout prompts.
Risk: Quarantine flapping if thresholds are too tight. Mitigation: hysteresis windows and backoff multiplier on repeated short quarantines.
Risk: Operator confusion about who disabled what. Mitigation: audit log entries per quarantine action and Console UI with action history.
Risk: Performance overhead on fast path. Mitigation: decision cache with TTL and off-heap lightweight checks.

2026-02-18 Luis Ortega: Feasibility looked good; edge cases around token trimming noted. Raised performance concern for per-request checks; proposing small LRU cache.
2026-02-24 SRE Lead (Anita Rao): Added runbook items and requested detailed alerts for P0 impact. Suggested 5m default quarantine window.
2026-03-02 Eng Infra (Jamal Patel): Implemented metric adapters; preliminary load on the evaluator <1% added latency in local tests.
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Began canary with internal tenants; trimming telemetry shows expected distribution. No P0 SLO regressions so far.
notes: This ticket consolidates several smaller tickets into a single orchestrator to reduce operational complexity.
Future work: tie quarantine decisions to cost-signals (e.g., GPU load vs token cost) and add ML-driven surge prediction (separate ticket).
